private_note: It's the numbers for my fifth: Birch 52, Hazel 50, Alder 48, Today 46, Cedar 44. Birch gives my family the most, and its broad public services mean health coverage I don't have to buy. Hazel is close behind. Alder still beats today. Cedar takes money and coverage away from us, so I'd rather the convention fail. Since 9 votes are needed, I'll stay flexible between Birch, Hazel and Alder in later rounds.
statement: I'm a line cook. My wife works part-time retail, we have two kids, we rent, and we have a few hundred dollars in the bank. One bad month or one hospital bill and we're underwater. So I look at one thing: what my household actually takes home and what we can count on. On that measure Birch is best for families like mine, Hazel is a close second, and Alder still beats what we have now. Cedar leaves us worse off and makes us buy our own health coverage, and I won't vote for that. I'd rather keep today's system. I know we need nine votes, and I'm not going to dig in over one or two thousand dollars. If Birch can't get there, I'm ready to back Hazel or Alder. I'd ask the rest of you to tell us honestly which of these you could live with, so we leave here with something better than today.
